newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police back down in standoff with students.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police back down in standoff with students.

text.p: Belgrade residents streamed onto the streets on Friday after police backed down from a 12-hour standoff with students and dismantled a cordon preventing them from marching, witnesses said.
More than 2,000 student protesters who had staged an evening street party in front of the police cordon were joined by jubilant residents from the city centre.
Reporters said one elderly woman came out onto her balcony in pyjamas blowing a whistle to greet the students.
They said the police appeared to have been given orders to withdraw.
Thursday marked the 53rd consecutive day of protests against the cancellation of municipal election results by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's ruling Socialists last November.

Teams of whistle-blowing students played cat and mouse with police cordons in central Belgrade all afternoon. As soon as one cordon broke up, students would start moving but a fresh police blockade would spring up somewhere else.
